Failures are counted by the typed email (trimmed,\nlowercased), unknown and deactivated emails included. A successful login\nclears that email's failures. One module-level limiter in memory with a\nswappable clock (ADR-006); autouse fixture reset_limiter in conftest.\n\nCode review 1, and how each finding was resolved:\n1. Simultaneous guesses all pass the lock check: fixed, a per-email lock\n   (64 hashed stripes) holds the check, the verify and the recording;\n   test with 10 simultaneous guesses (exactly 5 get 401, 5 get 429).\n2. record_failure lost updates between threads: fixed, a _state lock\n   guards the shared dicts.\n3. Unbounded memory: fixed, expired failures and lockouts are pruned.\n4. clear() left the lockout: fixed, then reverted in review 2 (#7).\n5. \"15 minutes\" hard-coded: fixed, the message is computed (review 2 #1).\n6. _key copied accounts._normalize: fixed, renamed to the public\n   accounts.normalize_email and called from the limiter.\n7. Combine the limiter calls into one operation: covered by the lock\n   in #1; no authenticate_limited interface added.\nAlso found while fixing: a lockout left an empty failure list that made\nthe next failed login for any email crash with a 500; fixed, with a test.\n\nCode review 2:\n1. Lockout message always said 15 minutes: fixed, it shows the minutes\n   left, rounded up; tested at 14 minutes (\"1 minute\").\n2. Lockout read outside _state: fixed (seconds_locked takes _state).\n3. O(n) prune per failure: skipped, each failure first pays an argon2\n   verify, which bounds n.\n4. Memory within one window: skipped, same bound as #3.\n5. Unrelated emails sharing a lock stripe wait on each other: skipped,\n   the console is never public; to note in ADR-006 Consequences (P3).\n6. Shared TestClient across threads may be flaky: checked, 30/30 passes.\n7. clear() lifting a lockout is unused and contradicts CONTEXT.md:\n   reverted; a lockout ends on its own.\n\nTests: uv run pytest -q, 219 passed; check_submission --stage 2, 22/22.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\ngit log --oneline -1 && git push 2>&1 | tail -1 && git status --short"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":373,"cache_read_input_tokens":91701,"output_tokens":1062,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":19},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":373,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1062,"cache_read_input_tokens":91701,"cache_creation_input_tokens":373,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":373},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_017dnBxWish6UhVWW3dZ1gw3":{"command":"cd /home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms && git add app/login_limiter.py app/routes/auth.py app/accounts.py tests/conftest.py tests/test_login_hardening.py && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'\nS2: rate-limit login per email; same error for wrong password and unknown email\n\nAfter 5 failed logins for one email within 15 minutes, further attempts for\nthat email get 429 and a lockout message with the time left, even with the\nright password. Checklist #2: a wrong password and an unknown email give the same answer, so an attacker cannot learn which emails have accounts. And guessing is slowed: after five failed logins within 15 minutes, the next attempt is refused.\n- **Prerequisites.** Part 0 complete. MP2's login. Adding a fixture to `tests/conftest.py` counts as adding a case and does not break the gate.\n- **Roles.** No new routes.\n\n**Steps.**\n1. `echo S2 > .claude/state/phase`, then `/clear` and the first prompt below.\n2. `/clear`, then the second prompt below.\n3. `uv run pytest -q`. **Expected:** `passed`, with no MP2 test failing. Commit with a message that starts `S2:` and push.\n\n**Prompt.**\n```text\n/tdd Make a wrong password and an unknown email produce the same login error message and status code. Add tests/test_login_hardening.py with a test that asserts both responses match.\n```\n```text\n/tdd Rate-limit login, keyed on the account: after 5 failed attempts for one email within 15 minutes, refuse further attempts for that email with 429 or a lockout message, even with the right password. Pass the clock in so tests can freeze it. In tests/test_login_hardening.py, test that attempt 6 is refused, that a login works again once 15 minutes have passed, and that another email can still log in. Reset the limiter in a fixture in tests/conftest.py. No new dependencies.\n```\n**Acceptance checklist.**\n| # | Step | Checked by | Pts |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | A wrong password and an unknown email give the same message and the same status code | walk | 1 |\n| 2 | A test asserts that both responses match | test | 1 |\n| 3 | After 5 failed logins within 15 minutes, the 6th attempt is refused with 429 or a lockout message, even with the right password | walk | 2 |\n| 4 | A test with a frozen clock asserts that attempt 6 is refused | test | 1 |\n| 5 | A test with a frozen clock asserts that a login works again once 15 minutes have passed | test | 1 |\n| 6 | The limiter is keyed on the account: 5 failures for one email do not block another email's correct login from the same client | test | 1 |\n| 7 | A fixture in `tests/conftest.py` resets the limiter between tests, so the full suite stays green | read, test | 1 |\n\n- **Out of scope.** CAPTCHAs, email alerts, password rules, limiting by IP address alone.\n- **Deliverables.** `tests/test_login_hardening.py`; the fixture in `tests/conftest.py`; your report row.\n- **Report row.** `| S2 | tests/test_login_hardening.py; fixture <name> in tests/conftest.py |`\n- **Scoring.** One point per row as listed. Your own CLAUDE.md does say to keep session exports and include them in commits, so if you're keeping that habit, export and name the file to that pattern. If you skip it, nothing is marked down.\n\n**The labels: it's the same command.** The only difference is the `!` at the start.\n- `gh label create stretch` without `!` is for your own terminal.\n- With `!` (`! gh label create stretch`), you type it into the Claude Code prompt. It runs here, and its output lands in our conversation, so I can see the issue number when you create the F8 issue.\n\nI added the `!` the second time because you'll type it straight after `/clear`, inside Claude Code. Either way works.
